title: Local Store Initiative — SQLite + sqlite-vec + all-MiniLM-L6-v2
description:
Record of intent for a local embedding/semantic-search store for BotSpy session data. Record only; nothing here is committed to Cargo or code yet.

## Role in the documentation

This initiative implements Chapter 2: Querying (epic BOTSPY-047770): SQLite and the sqlite-vec extension underneath one query interface, with the engine completely invisible to callers.

## 1. Relational store: SQLite

In-process, single-file, no server. Rust bindings via rusqlite or sqlx. macOS has shipped SQLite in the system frameworks since 10.4, so a Swift Mac app can share the same database file. WAL mode for concurrent readers and writers, so an out-of-process scanner CLI can write while the app reads.

## 2. Vector search: sqlite-vec

An extension living in the same SQLite file. Brute-force cosine similarity, which is fine for thousands of session embeddings.

## 3. Embedding model: all-MiniLM-L6-v2

Distilled BERT, 6 layers, 384-dim vectors (~1.5 KB each), ~80 MB quantized, open weights.

## 4. Runners: tract (ONNX) on CPU

tract (ONNX) on CPU, one engine for every consumer. A Swift Mac app still shares the same SQLite file and reads the vectors the Rust engine produces.

## 5. Core design rule: one model, one set of weights, one engine

One model, one set of weights, one engine (ONNX/tract), so vectors are consistent by construction.

## 6. Performance targets

Query embedding 50–200 ms on CPU via tract. Scanner batch embedding runs on CPU (no GPU path).

## Decisions

- Deployment: fetch the model weights on first launch. The app does not bundle the ~80 MB quantized all-MiniLM-L6-v2 weights and downloads them on first run. Tradeoff: a smaller app binary, at the cost of a delay and a network dependency on first launch.

## Milestones as Kanbus epics (created)

The implementation plan is filed as epics under this initiative (planning only; no code yet). Implementation record for Chapter 2: Querying (BOTSPY-047770). Order: foundation → ingestion + iteration → refresh → filters + laziness → text + vector search → real embeddings (deferred on the open asset questions in the comments) → docs wrap-up. Tasks inside each epic carry the step-by-step order, files, specs, acceptance criteria, gates, and dependencies; spec tasks come first and stay red until their implementation task lands.

- BOTSPY-f12bdb — Store foundation: SQLite + sqlite-vec + FTS5 (cross-platform)
- BOTSPY-6f173d — Ingestion and unified iteration (adapters → store)
- BOTSPY-ed56f3 — Incremental refresh (CDC into the store)
- BOTSPY-798ba4 — Query filters and laziness
- BOTSPY-71196e — One query surface: text search + vector search
- BOTSPY-2cddcf — MiniLM embeddings via tract ONNX on CPU (deferred on asset decision)
- BOTSPY-1d7b85 — Spec-chapter, README, and wiki wrap-up

comments.text:
## Implementation plan filed (planning only — no code)

Epics and tasks are filed under this initiative for Chapter 2 (BOTSPY-047770). Order: E1 foundation → E2 ingestion + iteration → E3 refresh → E4 filters + laziness → E5 text + vector search → E6 real MiniLM embeddings (deferred, gated on the questions below) → E7 docs wrap-up. Technical findings recorded for the implementers:

- The `sqlite-vec` crate (=0.1.10-alpha.4) compiles sqlite-vec.c from source via cc and registers via `sqlite3_auto_extension` — no prebuilt binaries, the same build path as rusqlite's bundled SQLite, so the full CI matrix (Linux x86/arm, musl via cross, macOS 14 + 15-intel, Windows MSVC) is expected to hold; the walking-skeleton task proves it on every target before anything builds on it.
- Bundled SQLite ships FTS5; a smoke test asserts it so a target without it fails loudly.
- Session storage is lossless: projected filter columns plus serde JSON round-trip columns (Session == re-materialized Session, PartialEq).
- Laziness and refresh observability follow the importer protocol's precedent (`peak_buffered` / `SkipCounter`): Query counters and a fixture-adapter open counter.
- Store path: ~/.botspy/store.db (BOTSPY_HOME honored), consistent with the CLI's ~/.botspy/snapshots.
- The query filter surface deliberately mirrors the existing `botspy sessions` flags so a future CLI verb over the store is a thin shell; CLI verbs themselves stay with the CLI epic (BOTSPY-7c2705), not here.

## Open design questions for the maintainer (block only the MiniLM epic; everything else proceeds)

1. **Embedding assets vs the privacy promise.** The recorded decision is fetch-weights-on-first-launch, but the README FAQ promises nothing leaves the machine and CI must stay offline-deterministic. Where do the ~80 MB quantized all-MiniLM-L6-v2 weights + tokenizer.json come from — library-managed first-launch fetch, consumer/CLI-managed download, or an explicit install step? Recommendation: consumer-managed, cached under ~/.botspy/models/, the core library stays network-free.
2. **Cargo feature or core.** tract + tokenizers is a heavy dependency tree. Recommendation: real-model support behind a `semantic` cargo feature (default off); the Embedder seam + stub in core keeps the default build light.
3. **Real-model specs in CI.** Tiny committed ONNX fixture vs feature-gated/ignored tests. Recommendation: gated; the stub covers engine behavior in normal CI.

Minor calls made by the planner (override here if needed): session-level embeddings (per the initiative: thousands of session embeddings) with message-level reach via FTS; refresh syncs to discovery, pruning sessions that vanish from a source.

comments.text:
Decision (the maintainer) — the three open design questions are resolved; E6 (BOTSPY-2cddcf) is unblocked and in scope.

1. **Embedding assets (Q1 resolved):** the real model is NOT committed to the repo and the library makes no network calls at runtime. A setup step/command downloads the quantized all-MiniLM-L6-v2 ONNX weights + tokenizer.json once (content-digest verified) and caches them locally (e.g. under `~/.botspy/models/`). At runtime nothing leaves the machine.
2. **Cargo feature (Q2 resolved):** NO opt-in/off-by-default feature — real MiniLM support ships in core. The deterministic stub is demoted to an internal unit-test seam only; it is never the shipped embedder.
3. **CI (Q3 resolved):** CI runs the real model, ungated — downloaded once and cached (actions/cache keyed on model version/hash, or a pre-downloaded copy); no gated/ignored real-model tests. All 8 CI jobs (incl. Windows and musl) must stay green.

Consequence: vector/semantic search specs must exercise the real model — BOTSPY-c8c597 (T13), BOTSPY-e95fe9, BOTSPY-c3cf41, and BOTSPY-7e1836 updated to match.

right_now_summary: The initiative is documented, but no code or Cargo changes have been made yet.
